html:
The 2022 FIFA World Cup was held in Qatar from 20 November to 18 December 2022, the first World Cup in the Arab world and the first in the Middle East.

Qatar won the right to host in 2010, in a vote later tied to corruption charges at FIFA, football's world body. Because of the summer heat, the tournament moved to the northern winter for the first time. Qatar spent huge sums on new stadiums and a metro, built mostly by migrant workers from South Asia and Africa. Rights groups reported many worker deaths and abuses under the kafala sponsorship system; the true toll is disputed.

On the field, Morocco beat Spain and Portugal and became the first African and first Arab team to reach the semi-finals. Argentina beat France on penalties in a 3 to 3 final, and Lionel Messi won the trophy he had long missed.

It was a showcase for a small gas-rich state, like Dubai with its towers, and follows the first World Cup of 1930 and the 2010 World Cup in South Africa.
sum: The 2022 FIFA World Cup was held in Qatar from 20 November to 18 December 2022, the first World Cup in the Arab world and the first in the Middle East.
